messages:
Mara: Heads-up — product asked for per-customer dashboards that show cost, latency SLOs, and noisy-neighbor signals. Need input from runtime/infra on what we can reasonably emit without exploding cardinality.
Sanjay: We can emit per-request labels: org_id, model, model_variant, region, GPU_pool_id, queue_ms, serve_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, batch_size.
Mara: Nice. Two constraints: 1) dashboards must not allow cross-org row-level access, 2) we want inexpensive pre-aggregations for high-cardinality orgs.
Jules: Agree. For observability pipeline we prefer pre-aggregated timeseries at these keys: (org_id, model, region) for latency percentiles, and global model-level for fine-grain percentiles. Per-request traces can keep full labels but go to a sampled index.
Lee: From product: rollouts UX needs to show per-customer SLOs so account teams can see regressions. Also we need an automated "noisy neighbor" badge when a customer is causing >20% capacity pressure. What's the signal for that?
Sanjay: Proposal: noisy_neighbor if org moving_average(queue_ms, 5m) > overall_pool_95th * 2 AND tokens_in_flight > pool_capacity * 0.15. That keeps it robust.
Mara: Sounds good. But how do we compute overall_pool_95th cheaply?
Sanjay: We can maintain pool-level aggregates (p50/p95) updated every minute from the same pre-aggregated stream. P95 computed from histogram buckets emitted by the runtime. Runtime can emit per-pool histograms with org_id omitted for pool-level ones.
Jules: Implementation note: histograms are fine, but we must cap unique org histogram writes to avoid cardinality hit. Strategy: full histograms for orgs in enterprise plan (opt-in), for others we emit binned counters + sampled traces.
Mara: That implies we need a flag on the account metadata: telemetry_level = [none|basic|detailed].
Lee: Product ok with that if basic covers dashboard KPIs and detailed gives full SLOs + traces. We'll include it in the admin UI.
Sanjay: Runtime change list: 1) add pool-level histogram metric (no org_id) 2) add per-request event with org_id and minimal labels (for basic) 3) optional detailed event with full labels for customers with telemetry_level=detailed.
Mara: What does "minimal labels" mean?
Sanjay: minimal = {org_id, model, serve_ms, queue_ms, tokens_in}. No GPU_id unless detailed.
Jules: On the ingestion side we need two pre-aggregation paths: timeseries rollups per (org_id, model, region) and pool-level rollups. Also a sampling pipeline for full traces stored to long-term storage for detailed customers.
infra-bot: deploy scheduled: metrics-schema-v2 -> staging at 2026-03-21T03:00Z
Mara: Example metric payloads for the runtime to emit (pseudo):
```
{
  "name": "inference.latency.histogram",
  "labels": {"pool":"eu-west-1-a"},
  "buckets": [0,10,50,100,250,1000],
  "counts": [123, 432, 210, 54, 12, 3]
}
{
  "name": "inference.request.event",
  "labels": {"org_id":"org_123", "model":"redwood-7b", "serve_ms":82, "queue_ms":10, "tokens_in":45}
```
Sanjay: We'll try to keep the per-request event under 300 bytes.
Lee: What about RBAC on dashboards? We must ensure org admins only see their org. Console team: advice?
Mara: Console will implement per-org scoping on the query layer — dashboard queries must include org_id filter scoped from the JWT. Also audit logs for any cross-org queries.
Jules: Also recommend a hard guardrail in the backend: deny queries with 'org_id = ALL' unless caller has an entitlement flag. Default list APIs will be scoped to the caller's org.
Mara: Quotas interplay — if a customer is rate-limited, should we still surface noisy neighbor badge? Might be confusing.
Sanjay: Noisy neighbor should ignore requests blocked by quota. Use only accepted requests and queued ones.
Lee: Action items:
- Mara -> mock a dashboard showing p50/p95, tokens, cost estimate, noisy_neighbor indicator (due EOD Tue).
- Sanjay -> PR to runtime to add pool histograms + per-request minimal event (draft by Fri).
- Jules -> update ingestion to pre-aggregate org/model/region timeseries and implement sampling policy (start next week).
- Console -> enforce org-scoped queries + admin entitlement check (sync with Mara).
Mara: I'll also add a short doc listing retained labels for each telemetry_level.
Jules: One more thing — retention and size. For detailed customers we may need longer retention for traces; product will decide on billing.
Lee: Noted. Communication plan: we'll post a short RFC in #eng-architecture and tag infra + console.
Sanjay: Quick question: do we need a synthetic "org_capacity" metric per pool so we can normalize noisy thresholds?
Mara: Yes. Runtime can emit pool_capacity tokens/sec and current_allocated_cores. Add that to the list.
Sanjay: Will do.
Mara: Thanks all :thumbsup:
alerts-bot: [sample alert] noisy-neighbor detected org=org_123 pool=eu-west-1-a score=2.3 (auto-generated for demo) :eyes:
